title: Random Variables
intro: A random variable is a number determined by the outcome of an experiment. Its distribution says how probability is spread over its possible values, and two numbers (the mean and the variance) summarise most of what matters.

blocks.text: Formally, a random variable is a function $X:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$. In practice you rarely look at $\Omega$ again: once you know the distribution of $X$, every probability about $X$ follows from it. This topic covers how distributions are described, how to compute with them, and how they change when the variable is transformed.

items: Discrete Random Variables (#/probability/random-variables/discrete): probability mass functions, distribution functions, indicators.
Continuous Random Variables (#/probability/random-variables/continuous): densities, the CDF, quantiles, and why $P(X = x) = 0$.
Expectation (#/probability/random-variables/expectation): the mean, linearity, LOTUS, indicator tricks and the tail-sum formula.
Variance and Moments (#/probability/random-variables/variance-and-moments): spread, standard deviation, skewness, kurtosis and higher moments.
Transformations (#/probability/random-variables/transformations): the distribution of $g(X)$, the change-of-variables formula, and turning uniform random numbers into any distribution.
